original_value: The notions of k-separability and k-producibility are useful and expressive tools for the characterization of entanglement in multipartite quantum systems, when a more detailed analysis would be infeasible or simply needless. In this work we reveal a partial duality between them, which is valid also for their correlation counterparts. This duality can be seen from a much wider perspective, when we consider the entanglement and correlation properties which are invariant under the permutations of the subsystems. These properties are labeled by Young diagrams, which we endow with a refinement-like partial order, to build up their classification scheme. This general treatment reveals a new property, which we call k-stretchability, being sensitive in a balanced way to both the maximal size of correlated (or entangled) subsystems and the minimal number of subsystems uncorrelated with (or separable from) one another.

result.paraphrase: The notions of k-separability and k-producibility are useful, expressive tools for characterizing entanglement in multipartite quantum systems when a more detailed analysis would be infeasible or unnecessary. In this work, we uncover a partial duality between them, which also applies to their correlation counterparts. This duality can be viewed from a broader perspective by considering entanglement and correlation properties invariant under subsystem permutations. These properties are labeled by Young diagrams, and we equip them with a refinement-like partial order to construct their classification scheme. This general framework reveals a new property, called k-stretchability, which is balancedly sensitive to both the maximum size of correlated or entangled subsystems and the minimum number of subsystems that are uncorrelated with, or separable from, one another.
